questions.question_text:
A triangle is rotated on the page without changing its size.
What happens to a chosen base and its matching perpendicular height?

options.text: Their directions change, but their lengths and right angle stay the same
The height becomes the longest side
options.why: Uses page orientation to relabel a side, ignoring the perpendicular relationship to the chosen base.

questions.solution_text:
A rotation preserves lengths and angles. The pair turns together, so the $90^{\circ}$ relationship remains.
Their directions change, but their lengths and right angle stay the same.

questions.question_text:
A parallelogram has area $96\,cm^2$ and base $12\,cm$.
The diagram labels a slanted side $m\,cm$.
What is the value of $m$?

options.why: Subtracting the base from the area does not determine a side length.
Dividing area by base gives the perpendicular height, not the slanted side $m$.
This does not follow from the given area and base.

questions.solution_text: Area equals base times perpendicular height, so $96/12=8$ cm is the perpendicular height. The labelled $m$ is a slanted side, and its length cannot be determined without an angle or more information.
